events_chronological: The lead barrister on a six-year class action defending a chemicals conglomerate stops taking his medication.
He strips during a deposition in a midwestern city and runs into the car park announcing that he is the servant of a corrupt design.
The firm's fixer, a ruined gambler, is sent out to bring him back.
The fixer, in debt to loan sharks over a failed restaurant, asks his partners for an advance against his bonus and is turned down.
The conglomerate's general counsel is briefed about the barrister and rehearses her answers alone in a hotel bathroom.
The barrister has obtained an internal memorandum showing the company knew its weedkiller was killing people.
He telephones one of the claimants and orders six hundred bound copies of the memorandum printed.
The general counsel authorises two contractors to put him under full surveillance.
The contractors kill him in his flat and dress it as a suicide by injection.
The fixer refuses to accept the suicide and finds the printer's receipt among the dead man's papers.
His brother's debts and his son's telephone calls close in on him from every direction at once.
He collects the annotated copy of the memorandum from the printers.
The contractors put a device in his car while he has stopped at the roadside to look at three horses in a field.
The car explodes, and he throws his watch and rings into the fire so the body will be taken for his own.
He confronts the general counsel at a board meeting, records her offering him money to keep quiet, and has the police waiting downstairs.
He gets into a taxi, hands the driver fifty dollars and tells him to just drive.
nonlinear_category_reason: Twelve of thirteen scenes run forward over four days; the exception is the car bomb, shown first and then reached in sequence after a caption sends the film back four days.
syuzhet_notes: The telling opens on the last night - the horses, the device, the explosion - and then a caption reading four days earlier sends it back to the start, after which it runs forward until it catches up with the fire.
fabula_notes: The dead lawyer's voice is heard over the opening, but it comes from a message left on an answering machine and belongs to a scene inside the chronology rather than to a frame outside it.
